FIX C APPLIED — r27 §6.7A2 ~L2386-2435 (new section BETWEEN §6.7A cross-refs and §6.7B source-freshness):
  - Heading: `### 6.7A2 LEADING CANONICAL — dbt ref() vs source() — the DAG-edge behavioral difference (NOT just a naming convention)`.
  - Numbered §6.7A2 to slot BEFORE §6.7B/K (the freshness canonicals that assume source() is understood) without disturbing the existing §6.7A-K alphabetic chain.
  - Keyword-anchor blockquote covering: dbt ref vs source, ref source difference, dbt DAG edge, source freshness entry point, when to use ref source, dbt dependency graph, dbt model vs source, stg_ FROM source, raw table dbt, hardcode table name dbt.
  - One-fact summary: ref() = another dbt MODEL (creates DAG edge, dbt builds upstream first, resolves relation name per target/schema). source() = RAW EXTERNAL input declared in sources: YAML (NOT built by dbt — graph's entry point), unlocks `dbt source freshness` + lineage.
  - Four-column distinction table (Refers to / Built by dbt / Creates DAG edge / Enables freshness).
  - Standard project rule: stg_ models select FROM source(); everything downstream uses ref(). Single chokepoint = stg_ layer.
  - Worked example: `models/_sources.yml` declaring `app.orders` with `loaded_at_field: ingested_at`; `stg_orders.sql` uses `{{ source('app', 'orders') }}`; `fct_orders.sql` uses `{{ ref('stg_orders') }}`.
  - Docs verbatim quotes for both ref() and source().
  - DO-NOT-WRITE quadruple: (1) ref() on a raw external table (use source()); (2) source() on a dbt model (breaks lineage, disables freshness); (3) hardcode `iceberg.analytics.tbl` for a model (breaks DAG + env portability); (4) bare relation name with no Jinja wrapper.
  - Cross-refs: §6.7B (freshness YAML), §6.7K (freshness CLI), §6.7D (seeds use ref(), not source()), §6.7E (unit tests' input: ref/source), dbt best-practices guide.
